chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the mature woman (thiyyib) who proposes marriage to herself, he said: She is more entitled to her own affair; she may manage her matter with whomever she wishes, provided he is a suitable match (kuf'), after she has previously married a man.

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: More entitled to her own affair (has greater autonomy)
key_terms.الثِّيِّب: Mature woman, specifically one who has been previously married and consummated the marriage
key_terms.تَخْطُبُ إِلَى نَفْسِهَا: She proposes marriage to herself (initiates the marriage contract)
key_terms.كُفْؤًا: Suitable match (equal in status, piety, etc.)

ai.seo_question: Does a previously married woman need a guardian to arrange her marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani highlights the juristic consensus in Shia fiqh that a mature, previously married woman (thiyyib) possesses independent agency (wilayah) over her marriage contract, unlike a virgin whose guardian typically acts on her behalf. The condition of 'kuf'' (suitability) ensures that her choice aligns with social and religious standards, reflecting the practical application of autonomy within the framework of familial oversight.
